facts.fact: Nigeria's Registrar General's Department told African registrars on 18 July 2026 that digital CRVS is operational in 36 states but only 15 states have ward registrars, with 3,372 wards activated and 304 registration workstations deployed; it gives no total of wards, and says the Commission will double the number to about 7,000 before the end of 2027.

The Registrar General's Department's presentation sets out the digital process and results for live births only: 14 million children registered in the last two years, and certificates issued in three days on average; it gives no death figure.

The Registrar General's Department describes civil registration offices set up in wards and local government areas where an officer registers and archives the birth on the platform, with real-time monitoring and reporting of registration data; it adds that offline functionality is essential in low-connectivity areas.
The Registrar General's Department lists a Digital CRVS Roadmap (2024-2026) beside the VITALREG platform and a national rollout strategy as its digitalisation approach.

The system is presented as Nigeria's own by the Registrar General's Department, with National Population Commission and local government functionaries certifying and registering births; it names sustainable financing as essential for nationwide scale-up without stating a source.

As of 18 July 2026 the Registrar General's Department reports expansion to the remaining 22 states under way, the platform having been launched by the Commission's chairman, and a plan to double activated wards by the end of 2027.
